request.goal: swim my first full length of a pool without stopping

plans.name: v1 #1

picture.line: Your body is a kayak: staying level and balanced lets you glide effortlessly, while fighting the water sinks the stern.
picture.name: a sleek kayak

notes: Best: it uses the brief's chapter titles exactly, and its hooks are curious. Worst: several outcomes are vague ('effectively', 'a clean breath') and the kayak picture is barely mapped.
Best: chapter titles follow the brief's outline and the hooks are honest; worst: the kayak picture has no part mapping and several outcomes are vague, such as "catch and pull water effectively".

plans.name: v1 #2

picture.line: Your body is a narrow canoe: press your chest down to keep the back afloat, roll gently along your long axis, and let your arms act as paddles.
picture.name: a floating canoe

notes: Best: good test-based outcomes such as six strokes and 15 m on a board. Worst: the hooks 'swimming slower than you walk' and 'fatigue faster than swimming hard' are shaky claims, the canoe picture is thin, and the day-28 target of 500 m is a big jump.

Best: crisp hooks such as "you never need to lift your head, only roll" and measurable outcomes; worst: it uses canoe instead of kayak with no mapping, and the claim "pressing your chest down" and "slower than you walk" go past the brief.

plans.name: v5 #1

picture.line: Your torso is the rigid hull resting flat on water, rolling smoothly from side to side rather than muscling upward.
picture.name: A sleek kayak

titles: Gear Up and Own the Shallow End
Float Flat and Stand Back Up
Roll to Breathe on the Side
notes: Best: the chapters follow the brief closely, and the day-7 outcome is clear. Worst: invented hooks ('most adult panics start with goggles', 'exhausts lungs faster than swimming hard') and a thin kayak picture.

Best: outcomes are concrete and the plan builds to combining kick, pull and breathing; worst: hooks make dubious claims like "most adult panics start with goggles" and "holding breath exhausts lungs faster than swimming hard", and the picture is thin.

plans.name: v5 #2

picture.line: Your buoyant lungs are the hull, your legs act as the steady rudder, and your arms are the rhythmic paddles.
picture.name: A slender kayak

notes: Best: the outcomes are sensible and the hooks stay close to the brief's facts. Worst: the kayak picture is vague and maps lungs, legs and arms inconsistently, and the day-28 claim of 'bilateral' breathing was never taught.
Best: it stays faithful to the brief's sequence and facts; worst: outcomes are vague ("pull efficiently", "relaxed pace") and the picture calls lungs the hull with no mapping.

plans.name: v6 #1

picture.line: Your body moves through water like a narrow kayak, where a level hull glides effortlessly and a tilted hull drags.

maps.is: the flat kayak hull skimming the surface
the stern rudder and small rear propeller
the dual-bladed paddle pulling clean through water
rolling the hull along its center axis without pitching up

picture.name: a touring kayak

notes: Best: the kayak picture has explicit maps and its hull-trim idea carries through the chapters, and the staged distance outcomes (3 m, 10 m, 25 m) are testable. Worst: the 'cut panic in half' and 'doubles the glide' hooks are invented claims.
Best: the kayak picture maps hull, kick, paddle and roll, and it carries through chapters such as "Trimming the Hull"; worst: made-up hook numbers like "cuts panic in half" and "doubles the glide".

plans.name: v6 #2

picture.line: Your body moves through water like a narrow kayak: when the hull sits level and rolls cleanly, propulsion takes minimal effort.

maps.is: the buoyant kayak hull that must stay flat on top of the water
the trim rudder that raises or sinks the back of the boat
the paddle blade catching water and pressing it straight backward
the steady stern motor keeping the vessel aligned and moving forward

picture.name: a touring kayak

notes: Best: the kayak picture has several mapped parts. Worst: the arm-stroke outcome says to swim 10 m 'while holding your breath', which contradicts the breathing lessons, and it makes up claims such as 'twice the forward thrust' and 'self-rescue' methods.

Best: the kayak picture maps hull, head, pull and kick and the outcomes are measurable; worst: it makes up claims like "twice the forward thrust" and a "10-meter swim while holding your breath", and its glide of 5 m is ambitious.
